last.verdict: Moderna swung to a $162 million quarterly profit and raised its 2026 sales outlook, helped by overseas COVID deals and a melanoma win. Cash is now far higher, partly from debt.

takeaways.label: Surprise profit, higher outlook
takeaways.text: Third-quarter sales rose 29% to $1.3 billion, mostly from overseas COVID vaccine deliveries, giving net income of $162 million versus a $200 million loss a year ago. Full-year sales growth is now seen at 15–25%, up from up to 10%.

takeaways.label: Cash picture transformed
takeaways.text: Year-end cash is now seen at $8.1–$8.3 billion, versus $4.7–$5.2 billion before. About $2.6 billion of that is net proceeds from new convertible debt. Spending guidance was also trimmed by about $0.2 billion.

takeaways.label: Melanoma win, flu launch
takeaways.text: The melanoma cancer shot cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% in a large trial run with Merck. The flu vaccine is approved but launching only in limited form this season.

takeaways.label: Norovirus still stalled
takeaways.text: No extra patients will be enrolled in the norovirus trial this season, and the company will talk to regulators about next steps. The flu/COVID combination shot still has no U.S. refiling path.

history.verdict: Norovirus vaccine setback outweighed a smaller-than-expected loss and lower costs.

reasons.label: Norovirus vaccine setback
reasons.text: Phase 3 norovirus vaccine missed early-success bar; more patients must be enrolled, delaying it.

reasons.label: Pipeline over numbers
reasons.text: Revenue is only $145M, so the stock trades on upcoming flu and melanoma news.

reasons.label: Cost cuts, cash runway
reasons.text: Spending outlook trimmed about $0.2B; year-end cash now seen at $4.7–5.2B.
